messages:
Maya: heads-up — small NDCG regression after PTQ bring-up for the new 3B reranker, ~1.9% on dev. throwing it here so we can triage quickly.
Sam: saw a similar blip in canary metrics, seems concentrated on short queries (<6 tokens). MRR also down but smaller.
Liam: can you paste a failing example (query + top candidates) and maybe tokenized outputs? helps rule out data drift vs model issue.
Maya: pasted one that consistently flips ranking:
```
query: "how to set up ci"
cand A: "...setup CI with github actions..." (score 0.73 before, now 0.58)
cand B: "...ci best practices, testing..." (score 0.66 before, now 0.69)
--- tokenizer outputs ---
A tokens: [101, 2003, 1037, 300, ... 405]
B tokens: [101, 2003, 1037, 300, ... 405]
```
Maya: those token lists look suspiciously identical because we concatenated docs naively with no separators for short candidates, so token offsets overlap. PTQ seems to amplify subtle score shifts.
Dez: infra note — we recently enabled a micro-optimization that de-duplicates identical token tensors across the batch to save memory. if two candidates tokenize to the same sequence we might be collapsing them for kernel reuse. could explain identical cache keys.
Sam: good catch. hypothesis: 1) token-level dedupe + 2) no doc separator -> KV cache reuse or identical attention patterns -> small scoring bias that pushes ordering on borderline queries after quantization noise.
Liam: simple repro: run eval harness with a forced separator token between candidates and compare. command I use: 
```
python eval/harness.py --model registry/small-3b-ptq --slice short_queries --inject_doc_sep "<DOC>" --output /tmp/sep_out.json
```
Sam: also try forcing deterministic quant backend (no kernel fusions) to check if quant bits are amplifying.
Maya: did a 1k-query short slice test this morning with sentinel injection + disable-dedupe flag. results: baseline (ptq-canary) ndcg@10 = 0.412, with sentinel ndcg@10 = 0.424 (+0.012), MRR +0.008. full-delta vs pre-ptq non-quant = -0.007 (much smaller than -0.019).
Dez: thanks — that points to a preprocessing/serving interaction rather than model architecture. I'll rollback the dedupe opt for canary and run a micro-benchmark.
Sam: long-term fix: always emit a non-tokenizable sentinel between candidates or include explicit doc-boundary special token in tokenization step. PR idea: add `preserve_doc_separators=True` to CandidateBatcher.
Liam: create a small unit test that ensures two different candidates never map to the exact same token-id sequence if they have different strings (unless identical text). catches broken dedupe.
Maya: action items: Maya -> open PR with sentinel + unit test; Dez -> revert dedupe in canary + confirm perf impact; Sam -> run 10k overnight sweep on validation and post summary tomorrow.
deploy-bot: PTQ-canary deployment rolled back to v2026-03-18_23:12 for ranker-small-3b (reason: observed ndcg regression). :wrench:
Maya: thanks — I'll hold new PTQ rollouts until tests and sentinel patch land. feel free to ping if you want help reproducing specific queries. :thumbsup:
Sam: i'll add a short eval slice to nightly CI to catch this class of regressions (short-query + candidate-token-equality).
Liam: noting this in the onboarding checklist for future models: explicit doc separators + dedupe-safety flag.
Dez: logging follow-up: I'll add an alert when more than X% of a batch shares identical token hashes so we can detect accidental collisions earlier.
Maya: nice. I'll upload the failing sample set to the rerank-evals bucket under /short_query_token_collisions/ so we can iterate.
